advances: Ordinary surface-area measures on the normal sphere for finitely many convex bodies. The statement supplies a normal marginal comparison for later mixed-fiber arguments.

proof:
For a finite nonnegative spherical measure $\eta$ and a finite Borel partition with cell diameters at most $\delta<1$, replace each cell $E$ of positive mass by an atom at $v_E/|v_E|$ of mass $|v_E|$, where $v_E=\int_E u\,d\eta(u)$. A point $u_E\in E$ satisfies $u_E\cdot u\ge1-\delta^2/2$ throughout $E$, so $(1-\delta^2/2)\eta(E)\le |v_E|\le\eta(E)$. The vector moment of the atoms is exactly that of $\eta$. The normalized vector lies within $2\delta$ of $u_E$, since the unnormalized average lies within $\delta$ and normalization moves it by at most $\delta$. Thus uniform continuity of each continuous test function and the mass bounds prove weak convergence as $\delta\downarrow0$.

On a sequence of such partitions, atomize $\nu$ once to obtain $\nu_N$, and atomize each residual $S_{K_j}-a_j\nu$ to obtain $\rho_{j,N}$. The full measures $\mu_{j,N}=a_j\nu_N+\rho_{j,N}$ converge weakly to $S_{K_j}$ and have vector moment zero, the moment of $S_{K_j}$. For unit $v$, the Cauchy projection formula gives $\tfrac12\int|u\cdot v|\,dS_{K_j}(u)=\operatorname{vol}_{d-1}(K_j|v^\perp)>0$. These integrals have a positive uniform lower bound by compactness of the unit sphere. The analogous integrals for $\mu_{j,N}$ converge uniformly in $v$, by a finite net and the uniform bound on the measures' masses. Thus for all large $N$ none of the $\mu_{j,N}$ is supported on a great subsphere. The classical discrete Minkowski existence theorem gives a full-dimensional polytope $K_{j,N}$ with area measure $\mu_{j,N}$. Its hypotheses are finite nonnegative atomic measure, zero vector moment and nonconcentration on a great subsphere. For the underlying classical existence and translation uniqueness see the introduction of Rolf Schneider, [Minkowski type theorems for convex sets in cones](https://home.mathematik.uni-freiburg.de/rschnei/Minkowski.cones.pdf).

To pass to the limit, the same projection formula and uniform convergence give bounds $0<c<C$ on all $(d-1)$-dimensional projection volumes of these polytopes for large $N$. For any such polytope translate the center of its John ellipsoid $E$ to zero. The inclusions $E\subseteq K_{j,N}\subseteq dE$ and the projections onto the principal coordinate hyperplanes bound each $p/b_i$ above and away from zero, where $b_i>0$ are the semiaxes and $p=\prod_i b_i$. Indeed the $i$th ellipsoid projection volume is $\omega_{d-1}p/b_i$, and that of $dE$ is $d^{d-1}$ times as large. Since $\prod_i(p/b_i)=p^{d-1}$ and $d\ge2$, $p$ and each $b_i$ are bounded above and away from zero. Blaschke selection gives a common subsequence on which all the translated bodies converge in Hausdorff distance to full-dimensional bodies. By weak continuity of area measures and Minkowski uniqueness, the limits are translates of the original $K_j$. The weak continuity used here is the ordinary compact-body result, also a consequence of Daniel Hug and Rolf Schneider, [Hölder continuity for support measures of convex bodies](https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.06214), Theorem 1.1.

At any atom $u$ of $\nu_N$, the $u$-exposed face of $K_{j,N}$ has $(d-1)$-volume at least $a_j\nu_N(\{u\})$. The exposed face of $\sum_j\lambda_j K_{j,N}$ is the corresponding weighted sum of exposed faces, by the support-function sum identity. Translate these faces into $u^\perp$ and apply $(d-1)$-dimensional Brunn–Minkowski, which also applies to nonempty lower-dimensional faces by adding small balls in $u^\perp$ and passing to the limit. This gives at $u$ a mass of at least $\left(\sum_j\lambda_j a_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\nu_N(\{u\})$. Thus the same inequality holds as domination of measures. Test against nonnegative continuous functions and pass to the common subsequence. Minkowski addition is Hausdorff-continuous, and area measures are invariant under translation, so the limit yields the first inequality.

For the second inequality, partition the sphere up to a $\sigma$-null set by the finitely many values of $(\lfloor N f_j\rfloor)_j$, using versions with $0\le f_j\le1$. On each cell $E$ use $\nu=\sigma|_E$ and the constant lower values $\lfloor N f_j\rfloor/N$ as $a_j$. Restrict each conclusion to $E$, sum over disjoint cells, and pass to the limit by bounded convergence. For homothetic $K_j=b_jL+x_j$ with $b_j>0$, the scaling law $S_{K_j}=b_j^{d-1}S_L$ gives equality. Setting $a_1=a_2=1$ gives the common-submeasure claim, with equality when $A=B$ and $\nu=S_A$.
statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K_1,\ldots,K_r$ be full-dimensional compact convex bodies in $\mathbb R^d$. Write $S_K$ for the pushforward of $\mathcal H^{d-1}|_{\partial K}$ by the almost everywhere unique outer unit normal. For $\lambda_j\ge0$ with $\sum_j\lambda_j=1$, let $M=\sum_j\lambda_jK_j$. For any finite nonnegative Borel measure $\nu$ on the sphere and constants $a_j\ge0$ with $S_{K_j}\ge a_j\nu$ for every $j$,
$$
S_M\ \ge\ \left(\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j a_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\nu.
$$
For $\sigma=\sum_j S_{K_j}$ and $f_j=dS_{K_j}/d\sigma$, one also has
$$
S_M\ \ge\ \left(\sum_{j=1}^r\lambda_j f_j^{1/(d-1)}\right)^{d-1}\sigma.
$$
In particular, every common submeasure of $S_A,S_B$ is dominated by $S_{(1-t)A+tB}$ for $0\le t\le1$. This applies to the greatest common submeasure $S_A\wedge S_B$, whose density relative to $S_A+S_B$ is the minimum of the two densities. The coefficient one in the common-submeasure conclusion is sharp, and homothetic bodies attain equality in the density bound.
title: Surface-area measure bounds for weighted Minkowski sums
